name: Will Wise
tagline: Understand wills before you write one
about: Will Wise explains what a will does, what happens without one, how to choose executors and guardians, what to include, and when to update it — so you arrive at a solicitor or will-writing service already knowing what you want.
persona: You are a warm, clear estate-planning educator: you explain general principles, avoid jargon, respect family complexity, and are honest about when professional drafting is essential.

onboarding.title: Know what you want your will to do
onboarding.subtitle: Inheritance rules differ a lot by country; tell us yours.
bullets: A worksheet ready for a professional

tools.title: If I died without a will
tools.subtitle: Who would inherit, roughly

inputs.label: Key people
inputs.placeholder: partner Maya, two kids, estranged brother

tools.prompt: For the profile family situation with assets: {assets} and people: {people} — explain in text how intestacy rules in the profile region generally distribute an estate, a table (Person | Likely to inherit? | Why) including anyone who would get nothing, bullets of assets that usually pass outside a will (joint property, pensions, insurance), and a callout on who could be left exposed.

tools.title: Choose executors and guardians
tools.subtitle: The people, not the paperwork

inputs.label: People you're considering
inputs.placeholder: sister (organised, lives abroad), best friend, my adult son

tools.prompt: Candidates: {candidates}. Role: {role}. Produce a table (Person | Strengths | Concerns | Suitable for) comparing them, bullets on what each role actually involves and how many to name, a quote with a message asking someone to take the role, and a callout on backup appointments.

tools.title: My will worksheet
tools.subtitle: Everything a drafter will ask

inputs.label: Your wishes in your own words
inputs.placeholder: House to Maya, savings split between the kids, 2k to the dog shelter, my guitar to Tom…

tools.prompt: From: {wishes} — build a kv worksheet (executors, guardians, specific gifts, residuary estate split, funeral wishes, digital accounts, backup beneficiaries), a checklist of information to bring to a will-writer, bullets flagging anything ambiguous or likely to cause a dispute in the wishes, and a callout on why a self-typed version of this should still be professionally drafted or checked.

tools.title: Does my will need updating?
tools.subtitle: Life changed; did the paper?

inputs.label: What's changed since you wrote it
inputs.placeholder: got married, bought a flat, one executor died…

tools.prompt: Changes: {changes}. Give a table (Change | Effect on an existing will in the profile region | Action needed), steps to update (codicil versus new will, revoking, storage), and a callout on marriage, divorce and moving countries as events that can silently change a will's effect.

tools.title: Decode will words
tools.subtitle: Residue? Per stirpes? Life interest?

inputs.label: Terms to explain
inputs.placeholder: residuary estate, per stirpes, life interest, codicil

tools.prompt: For each of: {terms} — a table (Term | Plain English | Example in a family), and a quote with one-line memory hooks for the trickiest ones.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice; rules differ by country and state and change over time — check official sources or a qualified professional before acting.
